title: Solving Quadratic Equations
seo_title: Algebra I Solving Quadratic Equations Worksheets (TEKS A.8A)
standard_text: A.8A solve quadratic equations having real solutions by factoring, taking square roots, completing the square, and applying the quadratic formula
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.8A: solve quadratic equations by factoring, square roots, completing the square and the quadratic formula, with word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Set to 0, then factor, take roots, complete the square or use the formula.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Factoring: set the equation to 0, factor, then set each factor to 0.
  • Square roots: x2 = 25 gives x = ±5.
  • Completing the square: add (b ÷ 2)2 to both sides.
  • Quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) ÷ (2a).

Examples

Example

x2 + 2x − 15 = 0

(x + 5)(x − 3) = 0

Answer: x = −5 or x = 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting ±x2 = 25 has two solutions.
Wrong signs from factors(x + 5) = 0 gives −5.
Dividing only part by 2aDivide the whole top.

faq.a: Solve quadratic equations having real solutions by factoring, taking square roots, completing the square, and applying the quadratic formula.
Factor if you can; otherwise use the formula.
b² − 4ac > 0: two solutions; = 0: one; < 0: none real.
The zero product property needs a product equal to 0.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 − 10x to make a perfect square trinomial?
items.e: Take half of −10 and square it: (−5)2 = 25. Then x2 − 10x + 25 = (x − 5)2.
Move −15: x2 − 2x = 15. Add 1 to both sides: (x − 1)2 = 16. Square root: x − 1 = ±4, so x = −3 or x = 5.
Move 7: x2 + 8x = −7. Add 16 to both sides: (x + 4)2 = 9. Square root: x + 4 = ±3, so x = −7 or x = −1.
Move 55: x2 + 16x = −55. Add 64 to both sides: (x + 8)2 = 9. Square root: x + 8 = ±3, so x = −11 or x = −5.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 − 2x to make a perfect square trinomial?
items.e: Take half of −2 and square it: (−1)2 = 1. Then x2 − 2x + 1 = (x − 1)2.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 − 8x to make a perfect square trinomial?
items.e: Take half of −8 and square it: (−4)2 = 16. Then x2 − 8x + 16 = (x − 4)2.
Half of 6 is 3. (x + 3)2 = x2 + 6x + 9, so subtract 9 to balance: −3 − 9 = −12. (x + 3)2 − 12.
Half of −12 is −6. (x − 6)2 = x2 − 12x + 36, so subtract 36 to balance: 10 − 36 = −26. (x − 6)2 − 26.
